_doc: Large batch L09 themed pass (TEMPLATE.md sections 9 and 10): saltwater gharial, delta gharial, alligator snapper, mire toad, elder mire toad, goliath frog, reef turtle, leatherback. New motifs live in motifs/large_L09.js (32, glyph/motion ids prefixed L09-, 5 custom chain effects: gharial cruising eyes-only with a V wake, a fish lured to the snapper's pink worm, the goliath frog's one huge leap with a splash, a hawksbill swimming over coral, a leatherback diving under and resurfacing). All 8 signature motifs are new and used by no other creature (100%). Sibling lends only as secondary motifs: tail-sweep and death-spin between the two gharials, fly-tongue, bog-breath and belly-flop from the mire toad to the elder. Reused from earlier catalogues where truly the same: bask-log, bog-gulp, wart-hide, bull-kick, gland-squirt (medium m07) and mud-flop, croak-ring (small). Every piece (unique, class and x0) has a hand note. The Sonnet family overrides in overrides/large/L09.json stay the Generic fallback; its three review flags are answered by the pictures: Fog Hush = marsh fog banks rolling out with a half-shut eye fading into them (puff), Sitting Smother = the rubbery granular hide bulging out and smothering (bash), Reef Shell = overlapping tortoiseshell scutes with a cleaner fish nibbling (shield).

saltwater-gharial.notes: Saltwater gharial of coast and wetland: a big grey-green crocodilian with a salt crust on its scutes and a very long thin snout lined with needle teeth, swept sideways through the water to catch fish; it lies for hours with only its eyes above water and spins in a death roll. It slides in low off the bank; teeth click on the strike, a hiss when it guards.

u0.n: Estuary Snap: the salt-crusted needle-toothed snout swings sideways along the edge through brackish water and snaps shut with a white star

u1.n: Death Spin: the long grey-green body spins over and over along the edge, dark back and pale belly turning, spray flung round

u2.n: Scute Ridge: three keeled bony scutes push up along the edge like spikes, salt crystals glittering on the keels

u3.n: Patient Float: only the raised eyes and the nostril knob sit above a water line along the edge, a slow blink, rings spreading

b0.n: Brine Gnash: the long snout lunges off the edge and gnashes, a glint running down the needle teeth

b1.n: Brine Sweep: the crested tail sweeps out from one side to the other, brine spray off the tip

b2.n: Brine Scales: rows of salt-crusted scutes line up along the edge and hold, crystals glinting

b3.n: Brine Spray: brine drops are flung off and fall, drying into little white salt cubes

x0.n: Brine Wallop: the heavy crested tail wallops out and drops back, a wet splat where it lands

delta-gharial.notes: Delta gharial of the river wetlands: an olive-tan gharial with a thin snout ending in the ghara, the pot-shaped knob that buzzes and blows bubbles; it drifts among the floating logs looking like one and naps on the sandbars. It bobs up as if floating; a bubbly buzz on the strike, a pop on guard and heal.

u0.n: Thin Snout: the thin snout with its round ghara knob buzzes bubbles, then drives the length of the edge with a strike star

u1.n: Death Roll: the muddy body rolls over off the edge, back and belly turning, river mud thrown up

u2.n: River Drift: logs drift out and back on the water... until two eyes open on one of them and sink again

u3.n: Log Nap: the gharial basks on a warm log, rising gently as it soaks up the sun

b0.n: Long-Nose Clamp: the ghara snout lunges off the edge and clamps, bubbles rising from the knob

b1.n: Mudbank Tail Sweep: the crested tail sweeps across the mudbank, clods flying

b2.n: Riverlog Plate: log after log lines up along the edge like a raft; one of them has eyes

b3.n: Mud-Gob Spit: gobs of river mud are spat off the edge and splat as they fall

x0.n: Mudbank Flop: the gharial flops out onto the mudbank and back, mud splatting up

alligator-snapper.notes: Alligator snapper of the wetland and coast: a huge turtle with a three-keeled spiked shell and a coat of weed, lying still on the bottom with its jaws wide open, wiggling a pink worm-shaped tongue lure until a fish swims in, then a crushing hooked beak. It rises up out of the mud; the beak cracks, a wet squish on guard and heal.

u0.n: Jaw Slam: the huge hooked beak gapes on its pink mouth, slams out and shut with a star and crack lines

u1.n: Mud Doze: the snapper dozes half sunk in the mud, only the spiked shell top showing, bubbles rising from its nostrils

u2.n: Weedy Hide: long weed strands wave off the spiked shell and scatter out and back, the snapper vanishing into the pond bottom

u3.n: Pink Lure: jaws gape at spot after spot, a pink worm tongue wriggling in each, until a fish comes close and they snap

b0.n: Bitter Chomp: the hooked beak lunges off the edge and chomps

b1.n: Mud Bank Thrash: the spiked keeled shell thrashes out off the bank, mud clods flying

b2.n: Keeled Shell: shells with three spiked keels line up along the edge like a mountain range, weed waving

b3.n: Worm Tongue Lure: gaping jaws hang at spots tied by thin pink lines, worm tongues wriggling as bait

x0.n: Waking Lunge: the old snapper wakes and lunges along the edge, beak first, bubbles streaming off it

mire-toad.notes: Mire toad of the wetland: a fat teal-green toad with warts and yellow poison glands, slick with slime, that belly-flops into the bog, breathes swamp gas and catches flies on a sticky pink tongue. It rises slow and wet; squish on the strike, a croak on guard and heal.

u0.n: Toad Slime: strings of slime stretch off the warty back like spikes, yellow glands shining, drops snapping off

u1.n: Belly Flop: a fat toad jumps up off the edge with its legs spread and flops flat on its belly, mud splashing out

u2.n: Bog Breath: bog-gas bubbles well up, swell and burst into stink curls that drift down off the edge

u3.n: Tongue Gulp: the sticky pink tongue shoots the length of the edge, catches a fly and reels it in

b0.n: Warty Gulp: a wide warty mouth lunges off the edge and gulps

b1.n: Sticky Tongue Lash: tongues lash off the edge, a fly stuck on the tip

b2.n: Wart-Crust Shell: dry crusty warts bump up along the edge and hold

b3.n: Mire Glandular Spit: gland slime strings drip off the edge and fall in drops

x0.n: Belly-Flop Slam: the fat toad slams out flat on its belly and drops back, a mud splat

elder-mire-toad.notes: Elder mire toad of the wetland: an ancient, enormous toad with moss growing on its back, huge warts and heavy half-closed eyes; it hardly moves, belches foul gas, mutters in the bog and hides in the marsh fog. It rises very slow and heavy; a deep croak on the strike, a hiss of fog on guard and heal.

u0.n: Slime Mantle: the mossy warty back lines the edge and holds, a sheen of slime running over the moss

u1.n: Mire Belch: the pale throat sac swells off the edge and bursts in a ring of foul green belch, spit flying

u2.n: Bog Mutter: low croak rings throb at spots, tied together by muttered lines

u3.n: Fog Hush: marsh fog rolls out in bands and back, the old toad's half-shut eye fading into it

b0.n: Fog Gulp: the old wide mouth lunges out and gulps a mouthful of fog

b1.n: Mire Tongue Flick: a slow old tongue flicks off the edge and still gets its fly

b2.n: Mossy Hide: moss sprigs push up off the warty back like a lawn and stay

b3.n: Lingering Gob: a gob of bog gas falls off the edge and lingers in a haze

x0.n: Patient Plop: after a long wait the huge toad plops out flat and back

goliath-frog.notes: Goliath frog of wetland and rainforest rivers: the biggest frog of all, sandy brown with a wide flat head and thick granular skin; it leaps huge distances, swallows crabs whole (pressing its eyes down to push them in) and shoves river stones into nest pools. It lands heavy with a thud; thud on the strike, a croak on guard and heal.

u0.n: Belly Slam: the giant flat-headed frog launches out and comes down splayed flat, a splash ring round it

u1.n: Gulp Down: a red crab is swallowed whole, the eyes press down to push it in and the frog rises refreshed

u2.n: Rubbery Skin: thick granular skin lines the edge, bulging under blows and springing back

u3.n: Sit Heavy: round river stones are shoved into a nest ring at spots, a pool fills and the frog sits heavy on top

b0.n: Haycart Gulp: the wide flat mouth lunges off the edge and takes a crab whole

b1.n: Hind Leg Kick: a huge hind leg kicks out off the edge

b2.n: Goliath Warty Hide: the warty granular hide holds along the edge, wet with river dew

b3.n: Sticky Spit: sticky spit squirts off the edge and drips

x0.n: Sitting Smother: the huge rubbery body bulges out over the edge, smothers and drops back

reef-turtle.notes: Reef turtle of the islands: a hawksbill with overlapping amber tortoiseshell scutes and a pointed hooked beak for picking sponges off the coral; it flies over the reef on its front flippers, sleeps wedged under ledges and cries salt tears. It hangs above the spot like over a reef and settles; a tink on the strike, a pop on guard and heal.

u0.n: Flipper Slap: a broad front flipper rises off the edge and slaps flat on the water in a burst of spray

u1.n: Reef Shell: overlapping tortoiseshell scutes line the edge like roof tiles, a yellow cleaner fish nibbling along them

u2.n: Drift Off: the hawksbill drifts up off the edge on slow flipper strokes, bubbles rising

u3.n: Beach Snap: the pointed hawksbill beak slams out and nips a sponge to bits

b0.n: Beak Snap: the hooked beak lunges off the edge and snaps

b1.n: Flipper Sweep: a flipper sweeps the length of the edge, water jetting off it

b2.n: Boulder Shell: the tortoiseshell sits like a boulder along the edge, kelp waving round it

b3.n: Brine Squirt: salt tears well up and drop off the edge, drying to salt

x0.n: Paddle Crush: the flipper paddles out hard and crushes down, a splat of water

leatherback.notes: Leatherback of island and coast: the giant sea turtle with no hard shell, a black leathery carapace with seven ridges and white spots, enormous front flippers it rows like oars; it dives deeper than any turtle and lives on jellyfish, swallowed past a throat full of spines. It rises floating and swaying as if swimming; flipper whirr on the strike, a pop on guard and heal.

u0.n: Ocean Glide: ridged spotted leatherbacks glide out on huge flipper strokes and come back

u1.n: Deep Slip: the shell outline shrinks into a dark ring as it slips down into the deep, glowing specks left behind

u2.n: Flipper Heave: enormous flippers row at spots tied together by lines of water, heaving the target off balance

u3.n: Oar Sweep: one enormous flipper rows round like an oar, slams out and drops back with a splash

b0.n: Leather Nip: a spotted beak lunges off the edge and gulps a pale jellyfish, the spiny throat showing

b1.n: Leather Flipper: a huge spotted flipper strikes out off the edge, a swirl off its tip

b2.n: Leather Shell: the ridged leathery backs line up along the edge, a sheen running over the white spots

b3.n: Leather Glide: the turtle glides down off the edge into dark water, bubbles and glowing specks

x0.n: Leather Oar Blow: the oar flipper drives the length of the edge, a jet of water behind it
